title: Elena Rybakina Advances at US Open, Nears World No. 1
seoTitle: Rybakina Advances at US Open, Nears World No. 1
subtitle: Victory over Jessica Bouzas Puts Kazakh Player Three Matches Away from World No. 1 Spot
excerpt: Elena Rybakina defeated Jessica Bouzas 6-2, 6-4 in the US Open second round, moving closer to the WTA No. 1 spot and a potential second Grand Slam title this year.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Elena Rybakina made headlines by defeating Spain's Jessica Bouzas in the second round of the 2026 US Open with a 6-2, 6-4 score. The result places the Kazakh player three wins away from reaching the top spot in the WTA world rankings.

Rybakina Overcomes Bouzas in Short Match

In the August 30th encounter, the aspiring world No. 1 broke Bouzas' serve twice in the first set and built a 5-2 lead in the second. Despite the Spaniard managing to tie it at 5-5, Rybakina regained the initiative and closed out the match in just over an hour.

Injury Recovery and Return to the Tour

This performance follows the Kazakhstani player's recovery from an injury that forced her to withdraw from the Cincinnati tournament. The player demonstrated full physical fitness by imposing her power game on the hard courts of Flushing Meadows.

Goal to Reach the Top of the Rankings

With this victory, Rybakina keeps alive the possibility of reaching the WTA's top spot. According to specialized press analysis, she needs to reach the US Open semifinals to surpass the current world No. 1, regardless of Aryna Sabalenka's results.

Impact on the Grand Slam Race

Winning the US Open would represent Rybakina's second Grand Slam title of the year, following the Australian Open, and would leave only Roland Garros as an obstacle to completing the Career Grand Slam. The player still needs to secure three more victories to guarantee her advancement in the tournament.

Outlook for Upcoming Rounds

Rybakina's next opponent has not yet been announced, but the victory reinforces her status as a favorite for the title. The tournament, which runs until September 13th, continues to attract the biggest names in world tennis, and Rybakina's performance will be crucial in defining the end-of-season calendar.
